ai.description: *Ghatixalus magnus* is a large tree frog (60–70 mm) with a pale brown dorsum featuring dark brown blotches. It is distinguished by its translucent, bluish-white belly and prominent, granular skin texture.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ghatixalus magnus* is best distinguished by its significantly larger body size (reaching over 60 mm) compared to other *Ghatixalus* species, which remain notably smaller.
ai.habitat: *Ghatixalus magnus* inhabits evergreen forests and riparian zones within the Western Ghats, typically at high altitudes ranging from 1,000 to 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Large-sized Ghat Tree Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged against mossy rocks and vegetation during the day to avoid detection by predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ghatixalus magnus* breeds during the monsoon, laying a single clutch of approximately 150–200 eggs in gelatinous masses attached to vegetation overhanging forest streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ghatixalus magnus* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting high-altitude evergreen forests above 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Ghatixalus magnus* is a series of high-pitched, pulsed notes emitted by males perched on vegetation near fast-flowing forest streams.
